first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and prior evidence indicates that simplifying signup and shortening onboarding durably improved completion, time-to-value, and early adoption. This directly addresses the current bottleneck without relying on retention-risky price promotions. Verify the underlying onboarding and signup records before committing to scope, segment, and success criteria.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening the post-signup onboarding flow for self-serve accounts, prioritizing removal or deferral of nonessential steps rather than broadly removing signup qualification fields. This directly addresses the 4% onboarding-completion decline and 6% activation decline. The verified shortened-flow result improved completion (+13%), time-to-value (-2.1 days), and 30-day retention (+3%), supporting sustainable qualified revenue. The SMB signup-simplification result also supports activation and qualified-revenue upside, but its 30-day retention decline (-1%) warrants monitoring qualification, retention, and qualified revenue alongside completion and activation.
